messages:
maya: we just got 4 OOMs in prod-us-west-2 during a spike (10:23). KV cache grew fast and batching latency spiked and then a couple of alloc failures
infra-bot: alert: OOM x4 service=model-serve-v3 region=us-west-2 link=https://internal/alerts/ALRT-2028-112
liam: quick triage: probable causes = KV cache growth + large concat batching + workspace oversize. Options: soft-reserve, reduce slab, KV TTL, batch window down
maya: soft-reserve? where's that flag?
tom: it's `allocator.soft_reserve_mb`. set to 128 to keep a headroom. also `cuda_allocator.slab_mb=192` helps reduce fragmentation.
liam: propose low-risk steps (apply sequentially):
1) set kv_cache.eviction_policy=LRU and kv_cache.max_prefix_age=600
2) set batching.window_ms=30 and batching.max_batch_items=6
3) set allocator.soft_reserve_mb=128 and cuda_allocator.slab_mb=192
4) enable runtime.fast_fallback=true with fallback-model=small-quant
maya: I'll run #1 and #2 now. Command:
```
/ops config set service=model-serve-v3 --env prod \\
  kv_cache.eviction_policy=LRU \\
  kv_cache.max_prefix_age=600 \\
  batching.window_ms=30 \\
  batching.max_batch_items=6
```
infra-bot: config apply started by maya (rev 421). see https://internal/deploys/421
tom: for #3 and #4 I can push a gated rollout. Also add a temporary circuit breaker: `circuit_breaker.long_seq_threshold=0.15` to fail long-running requests early.
liam: while rolling, add kernel selection tracing so we can see if the big kernels (fused-attn-64) were picked. `diag.kernel_trace=on`
maya: KV prune kicked in, cache size dropped ~40% in 3m. batching median went from 60ms -> 22ms. no new OOMs for 8m :thumbsup: 
sre-oncall: keep 20m watch. collect allocator snapshots + kernel_trace logs and attach to INC ticket. If OOMs return escalate to full rollback.
liam: note for postmortem: consider adjusting batching concat heuristic to limit per-request token concat and prefer prefixed KV reuse thresholds. Also investigate using buffer_reuse=true but only with slab_mb small to avoid growth.
tom: copied. I'll prepare a follow-up perf run in staging with varying slab_mb and soft_reserve values to find sweet spot.
maya: attaching allocator-snap-10-23.log and kernel-trace-10-23.log to https://internal/incidents/INC-2028-22
infra-bot: monitor: no new alerts for 12m. closing alert thread if stable.
maya: closing for now, will open a short postmortem tomorrow with suggested defaults.
